searchText: Hi <@199561711278227457> , what tools are used to generate genesis states for test nets? We are wondering if we're at a point now that we can delete "start from deposits" code and just always assume a genesis state in the db. This would open up a lot of cleanup opportunities. I'm mainly using proto's `eth2-testnet-genesis` tool ( https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-testnet-genesis). I just tested lighthouse with its `merge` state and it worked flawlessly, so it recognized the validators and didn't need to start deposit processing. I guess you're talking about prysm using the same approach? command used to generate the merge state: `eth2-testnet-genesis --config config.yaml --mnemonics menmonics.yaml --eth1-config genesis.json --tranches-dir /output --state-output /output` tagging <@892053833121923094> in case the change affects hive Do you have docs or scripts you can share that you use when you run through the process? We have an e2e framework that starts pre-genesis, which we'll need to update to use this approach before we remove any of the pre-genesis code. sure, I can send them across that would be wonderful, thank you! I just saw this https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/11508 👍

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
I'm mainly using proto's `eth2-testnet-genesis` tool ( https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-testnet-genesis). I just tested lighthouse with its `merge` state and it worked flawlessly, so it recognized the validators and didn't need to start deposit processing. I guess you're talking about prysm using the same approach?

command used to generate the merge state:
`eth2-testnet-genesis --config config.yaml --mnemonics menmonics.yaml --eth1-config genesis.json --tranches-dir /output --state-output /output`

tagging <@892053833121923094> in case the change affects hive
